references.text: Pharaoh gives a command concerning Abram and sends him away with his wife, parallel to how a foreign ruler issues a command regarding the patriarch and his wife.
God prevented Abimelech from touching (נגע) Sarah and commanded him to return her – parallel to Abimelech's command that anyone who touches (נגע) Isaac or his wife shall die.
The one who goes in to another man's wife shall not go unpunished – reflects Abimelech's warning of the death penalty for anyone who touches Isaac or Rebekah.
The warning that whoever touches (נגע) the mountain shall surely die (מוֹת יוּמָת), using the same wording as Abimelech's command regarding the death penalty.
Connects two events where a king pronounces a death sentence on an entire family, but with conflicting moral character (protection versus unjust mass death).
Shows continuity in Abimelech's fear of God's judgment concerning the patriarchs' wives, moving from passive warning to active protection.
